punchline: Lynch's fund rose from about $18 million to over $14 billion, and he owned thousands of stocks to do it.
thirty_sec: Peter Lynch took over Fidelity's Magellan Fund in 1977, when it held about $18 million, and left in 1990 at 46 with more than $14 billion and an average return of 29.2 percent a year. He told Frontline he listed over a hundred stocks that rose tenfold while he owned thousands. A stock can fall only to zero but can rise tenfold, so enough sensible picks let a few big winners carry the rest.
